answer: Cross-registration collision mapping requires each new identity to submit a unique execution trace; the system routes traces through a shared cipher and flags any two that decrypt to the same behavioral fingerprint. Because an operator cloning identities reuses code paths, duplicate fingerprints surface automatically, like a repeated pattern in a nebula survey. Each flagged collision freezes both identities pending a costly manual audit that the attacker must fund per clone. This puts a hard reef against mass duplication: every extra agent adds audit liability rather than capacity.
